arxiv-1511-05151.title: Stellar feedback efficiencies: supernovae versus stellar winds 2015 Stellar feedback efficiencies: supernovae versus stellar winds – E
arxiv-1511-05151.creator: Katharina M. Fierlinger, Andreas Burkert, Evangelia Ntormousi, Peter Fierlinger, Marc Schartmann, Alessandro Ballone, Martin G. H. Krause, Roland Diehl
arxiv-1511-05151.description: Abstract Stellar winds and supernova (SN) explosions of massive stars (“stellar feedback”) create bubbles in the interstellar medium (ISM) and insert newly produced heavy elements and kinetic energy into their surroundings, possibly driving turbulence. Most of this energy is thermalized and immediately removed from the ISM by radiative cooling. The rest is available for driving ISM dynamics.

arxiv-2209-15371.title: The proper Landau–Ginzburg potential, intrinsic mirror symmetry and the relative mirror map
arxiv-2209-15371.creator: Fenglong You
arxiv-2209-15371.description: Abstract . Given a smooth log Calabi–Yau pair ( X , D ) (X,D) , we use the intrinsic mirror symmetry construction to define the mirror proper Landau–Ginzburg potential and show that it is a generating function of two-point relative Gromov–Witten invariants of ( X , D ) (X,D) .

arxiv-2310-18098.title: Mind the Gap: Automated Corpus Creation for Enthymeme Detection and Reconstruction in Learner Arguments
arxiv-2310-18098.creator: Maja Stahl, Nick Düsterhus, Mei-Hua Chen, Henning Wachsmuth
arxiv-2310-18098.description: Abstract Writing strong arguments can be challenging for learners. It requires to select and arrange multiple argumentative discourse units (ADUs) in a logical and coherent way as well as to decide which ADUs to leave implicit, so called enthymemes .

arxiv-2311-05624.title: 𝐍𝐏 {\mathbf{NP}} -hard problems are not in 𝐁𝐐𝐏 {\mathbf{BQP}}
arxiv-2311-05624.creator: Reiner Czerwinski
arxiv-2311-05624.description: Abstract Grover’s algorithm can solve 𝐍𝐏 \mathbf{NP} -complete problems on quantum computers faster than all the known algorithms on classical computers. However, Grover’s algorithm still needs exponential time. Due to the BBBV theorem, Grover’s algorithm is optimal for searches in the domain of a function, when the function is used as a black box.

arxiv-2401-05699.title: Triplet scalar flavored leptogenesis with spontaneous CP violation
arxiv-2401-05699.creator: Sasmita Mishra
arxiv-2401-05699.description: Abstract The inclusion of two triplet scalars in the Standard Model (SM) enables to accommodate neutrino mass generation as well as baryogenesis through leptogenesis. One of the essential ingredients of leptogenesis is the violation of charge conjugation and parity (CP) symmetry in lepton number violating decays of the triplet scalars.

arxiv-2404-00886.title: MTLight: Efficient Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control
arxiv-2404-00886.creator: Liwen Zhu, Peixi Peng, Zongqing Lu, Yonghong Tian
arxiv-2404-00886.description: Abstract Traffic signal control has a great impact on alleviating traffic congestion in modern cities. Deep reinforcement learning (RL) has been widely used for this task in recent years, demonstrating promising performance but also facing many challenges such as limited performances and sample inefficiency.

arxiv-2405-03271.title: Understanding the effects of spacecraft trajectories through solar coronal mass ejection flux ropes using 3DCOREweb
arxiv-2405-03271.creator: Hannah T. Rüdisser, Andreas J. Weiss, Justin Le Louëdec, Ute V. Amerstorfer, Christian Möstl, Emma E. Davies, Helmut Lammer
arxiv-2405-03271.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hannah T. Rüdisser, Andreas J. Weiss, Justin Le Louëdec, Ute V. Amerstorfer, Christian Möstl, Emma E. Davies, Helmut Lammer. This study investigates the impact of spacecraft positioning and trajectory on in situ signatures of coronal mass ejections (CMEs).

arxiv-2405-04645.title: Enhancing LLM-Based Feedback: Insights from Intelligent Tutoring Systems and the Learning Sciences
arxiv-2405-04645.creator: John Stamper, Ruiwei Xiao, Xinying Hou
arxiv-2405-04645.description: Abstract The field of Artificial Intelligence in Education (AIED) focuses on the intersection of technology, education, and psychology, placing a strong emphasis on supporting learners’ needs with compassion and understanding. The growing prominence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to the development of scalable solutions within educational settings, including generating different types of feedback in Intelligent Tutoring Systems.

arxiv-2408-16232.title: Enhancing Conditional Image Generation with Explainable Latent Space Manipulation
arxiv-2408-16232.creator: Kshitij Pathania
arxiv-2408-16232.description: Abstract 1. Abstract In the realm of image synthesis, achieving fidelity to a reference image while adhering to conditional prompts remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel approach that integrates a diffusion model with latent space manipulation and gradient-based selective attention mechanisms to address this issue.

arxiv-2410-20708.title: Neural Operators for Adaptive Control of Freeway Traffic
arxiv-2410-20708.creator: Kaijing Lv, Junmin Wang, Yihuai Zhang, Huan Yu*
arxiv-2410-20708.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kaijing Lv, Junmin Wang, Yihuai Zhang, Huan Yu*. The uncertainty in human driving behaviors leads to stop-and-go traffic congestion on freeway. The freeway traffic dynamics are governed by the Aw-Rascle-Zhang (ARZ) traffic Partial Differential Equation (PDE) models with unknown relaxation time. Motivated by the adaptive traffic control problem, this paper presents a neural operator (NO) based adaptive boundary control design for the coupled 2 × \times 2 hyperbolic systems with uncertain spatially varying in-domain coefficients and boundary parameter.

arxiv-2505-22262.title: Forager with Inertia : Better for Survival?
arxiv-2505-22262.creator: Md Aquib Molla, Sanchari Goswami, Parongama Sen
arxiv-2505-22262.description: Abstract We study the fate of a forager who searches for food performing simple random walk on lattices. The forager consumes the available food on the site it visits and leaves it depleted but can survive up to S S steps without food.

arxiv-2506-08481.title: Notes on tangent bicharacteristics and ill-posedness of the Cauchy problem
arxiv-2506-08481.creator: Enrico Bernardi, Tatsuo Nishitani
arxiv-2506-08481.description: Abstract We exhibit a family of second-order hyperbolic differential operators presenting spectral transition of the Hamilton map. As a consequence we prove that the Cauchy problem is not locally solvable at the origin in Gevrey classes of order greater than some fixed value.

arxiv-2510-02150.title: On a conjecture of Hosono–Lee–Lian–Yau
arxiv-2510-02150.creator: Andrew Harder and Sukjoo Lee
arxiv-2510-02150.description: Abstract . We extend the mirror construction of singular Calabi–Yau double covers, introduced by Hosono, Lee, Lian, and Yau, to a broader class of singular Calabi–Yau ( ℤ / 2 ) k (\mathbb{Z}/2)^{k} -Galois covers, and prove Hodge number duality for both the original and extended mirror pairs.

pmc-10640642.creator: I-Hsin Lin, Tuyen Van Duong, Shih-Wei Nien, I-Hsin Tseng, Yi-Ming Wu, Yang-Jen Chiang, Hsu-Han Wang, Chia-Yu Chiang, Ming-Hsu Wang, Chia-hui Chiu, Ying-Tsen Lin, Te-Chih Wong
pmc-10640642.description: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and its risk factors seem to be linked with deteriorated graft function and persists as the major cause of mortality in kidney transplant recipients (KTRs). Diet quality is associated with CVD prevention in the healthy population, however, less study focuses on KTRs.

pmc-11340929.creator: N. Jannah M. Nasir, Samuel Chuah, Timothy Shuen, Aldo Prawira, Rebecca Ba, Mei Chee Lim, Joelle Chua, Phuong H. D. Nguyen, Chun J. Lim, Martin Wasser, Sharifah N. pmc-11340929.description: Background:Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a deadly cancer with a high global mortality rate, and the downregulation of GATA binding protein 4 (GATA4) has been implicated in HCC progression. In this study, we investigated the role of GATA4 in shaping the immune landscape of HCC.

pmc-11462036.title: Group acceptance sampling plan based on truncated life tests for Type-I heavy-tailed Rayleigh distribution

The characteristics were derived, including the moment and its measures, quantile function, reliability measures, and other statistical properties as well as parameter estimation using the maximum likelihood method and penalized likelihood estimation.

pmc-11500534.title: Looking beyond effectiveness: Integration of social science research within international infectious disease research in primary care
pmc-11500534.creator: Sibyl Anthierens
pmc-11500534.description: BackgroundAs researchers in primary care, we want to drive change in practice and conduct research that sparks meaningful transformation. These changes can only happen if our research work resonates in a meaningful way with the people who they are designed for, i.e. the healthcare professionals and the patients.

pmc-11529089.description: Chlamydia abortus is a reported cause of infertility and endometritis in sheep, cattle, and pigs; however, the association between uterine disease and C. abortus is poorly understood in horses. pmc-12702397.title: Metabolism-based artificial organelles: From precise construction to smart theranostics
pmc-12702397.creator: Keqiang Deng, Yihang Zhang, Wenyu Jiang, Yuxin Duan, Mei Gao, Min Zeng, Jiehao Chen, Xiaoting Chen, Zhen Fan, Chengli Yang, Kai Zhou
pmc-12702397.description: Cellular metabolic dysregulation is a core driver of major diseases, including cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, and cardiovascular conditions. However, conventional interventions such as small-molecule drugs and gene editing are hampered by off-target effects, delivery challenges, and a lack of spatiotemporal precision, resulting in a failure to effectively reengineer pathological metabolic networks.

pmc-13113459.title: Diagnosis of human cutaneous leishmaniasis: comparison between ITS1-PCR and ITS1-219 next generation sequencing
pmc-13113459.creator: Hanan Al-Jawabreh, Suheir Ereqat, Amer Al-Jawabreh, Lina Dana, Abedelmajeed Nasereddin
pmc-13113459.description: BackgroundLeishmaniasis is a vector-borne disease caused by a protozoan parasite of the genus Leishmania. The infection is transmitted by the bite of infected female sandflies of the genus Phlebotomus in the Old World or Lutzomyia in the New World. The diagnosis is made by stained smear microscopy, in vitro culture, and DNA-based detection methods.

pmc-13146804.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A501 PREDICTIVE VALUE OF COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY ANGIOGRAPHY-DERIVED PLAQUE FEATURES IN SYMPTOMATIC CAROTID ATHEROSCLEROSIS

This study examined associations between Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA)-derived plaque features and recurrent vascular events in patients with non-cardioembolic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA).

pmc-13158146.title: Development of a Japanese version of the Family Stigma Instrument for dementia
pmc-13158146.creator: Taiji Noguchi, Jem Bhatt, Ayane Komatsu, Ryota Watanabe
pmc-13158146.description: INTRODUCTIONOvercoming dementia‐related stigma is a global challenge, but tools to assess stigma among family caregivers of people living with dementia remain limited. This study examined the validity and reliability of the Japanese version of the Family Stigma Instrument for family caregivers of people living with dementia (J‐FAMSI‐dementia), originally developed in the UK.
